title: Real L2 completeness and integral Cauchy–Schwarz
statement: Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. For integers $m\geq1$ and $r\geq0$, let $L^2(\mathbf R^m,\mathbf R^r)$ be the space of Lebesgue-measurable functions modulo almost-everywhere equality with finite integral of the squared Euclidean norm. With inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int_{\mathbf R^m}\langle u(x),v(x)\rangle\,dx$, this is a complete real inner product space; in particular every Cauchy sequence for $\|u\|_2=(\int\|u(x)\|^2\,dx)^{1/2}$ has an $L^2$ limit. The integral inner product is absolutely integrable and $|\langle u,v\rangle_2|\leq\|u\|_2\|v\|_2$. For real scalar $a,b\in L^2(\mathbf R^m,\mathbf R)$ one also has $\int|a(x)b(x)|\,dx\leq\|a\|_2\|b\|_2$.

The norm identity is the inner-product-space norm_sq_eq_re_inner axiom with inner_def. norm_inner_le_norm in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean:453 gives Cauchy–Schwarz. Apply that same scalar L2 inequality to |a| and |b| for the last clause: their L2 norms equal those of a and b by the displayed norm formula. No condition r>0 is needed.
